items.title: 13.10.1 Reaction with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide

source_refs.note: Topic 13.10.1 with the Keep in Mind box, printed page 300.

blocks.text: Chlorine undergoes disproportion when it reacts with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH) forming sodium chloride (NaCl) and sodium chlorate (I) (NaClO).
Oxidation states of chlorine in the above reaction are given below:

blocks.title: Keep in Mind!
blocks.text: Sodium chlorate (I) is previously called sodium hypochlorite.
Chlorine in Cl₂ is oxidized from 0 to +1 in NaOCl. Chlorine in Cl₂ is reduced from 0 to 1 in NaCl.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says chlorine is reduced from 0 to 1 in NaCl; the minus sign is missing. Chlorine in NaCl is -1, so it is reduced from 0 to -1.
The above reaction shows the simultaneous oxidation and reduction of chlorine and is example of disproportionation reaction.
